_comment: Noble's real Universal Print registration, captured from the Azure portal on
Overview, Properties > Printer defaults, and Connectors).
These are RESOURCE IDENTIFIERS, not credentials: they name objects inside the
tenant and are useless without a token. The printer share id is a routine
request parameter Power Automate passes on every call. No secret is here.
Why it earns a place in the suite: the printer id and the share id are two
DIFFERENT GUIDs, and mixing them up is exactly defect F3 -- Resubmit cancelled
against the wrong one, got a 404, and reported a clean cancel while the
original job stayed alive to print twice. With both real values here, that
class of mistake fails with a legible diff instead of two lookalikes.
DATE NOTE, so nobody 'corrects' it: the prose above says 2026-08-30 and the
ISO fields below say 2026-08-31. Both are right. The instants are UTC, as
America/Vancouver, which is the clock this project renders Print_Message in.

status._source: CORRECTED 2026-08-30 from the live API via live-printer-check.ps1.
_note: The API returns 'idle'. The PORTAL displays 'Ready'. They are not the
same string, and an earlier revision of this file recorded the portal's
display text as if it were an API value -- so two tests asserted a state
Graph never returns. printerProcessingState is documented as
unknown | idle | processing | stopped; 'ready' is not a member.

_source: RE-SHARED 2026-08-31 16:14 UTC. The printer share was deleted and created
again in the portal, which MINTS A NEW SHARE ID. The old one,
5de37377-8b08-459f-b7a6-670349acb4f7, is dead: Graph answers it with
404 'The printer share id ... does not match any registered printers.'
The PRINTER id did not change and cannot -- registeredDateTime above is
still 2026-08-28. That asymmetry is the point worth remembering: the id
this pipeline passes on every call (the share) is the volatile one, and
the id it never receives from the caller (the printer, resolved at
preflight) is the stable one. Anywhere the share id is written down --
README, docs, this fixture, the Power Automate Flow bodies, the
live-printer-check.ps1 default -- goes stale the moment someone re-shares.
So a 404 on the share route means 'look up the share id again', NOT

capabilities._source: CORRECTED 2026-08-30 from the live API via live-printer-check.ps1.
_note: contentTypes is the CAPABILITY list and holds TWO entries. An earlier
revision recorded only application/pdf, taken from the portal's
Properties > Printer defaults page -- but that page shows the DEFAULT
content type, not everything the device accepts. capabilities and
defaults are different objects and the portal does not label which is
which. Read capabilities from the API, never from a settings page.
What matters for this pipeline is unchanged and now verified against the
service rather than a screenshot: application/pdf IS supported, so the
PDFs pulled out of SharePoint go straight to the device with no OXPS
conversion.
'Fit PDF to page' and 'Multipage layout' are GREYED OUT in the portal --
the device does not support them. JOB_CONFIGURATION must never start
sending either; test_real_printer.py asserts that.

connectors._source: CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 by live-printer-check.ps1 -DiagnoseOnly: 0 connectors on this printer AND 0 in the whole tenant.
_note: SETTLED 2026-08-30: this printer is UNIVERSAL PRINT READY and registered
DIRECTLY. No connector is needed and none exists.
How it was settled -- by measurement, not inference. scripts/
live-printer-check.ps1 submitted a real job while the API reported 0
connectors on this printer AND 0 across the entire tenant. Job id 6 went
pending -> processing -> completed in about five seconds and a page came
out of the tray. Nothing could have been bridging it, so the service is
talking to the device itself.
Two earlier answers are kept here because both were wrong in instructive
ways. The first claimed this was confirmed by the Overview blade reading
'Last seen: 2 minutes ago / Ready / accepting jobs' -- it was not: a
connector's heartbeat updates last-seen exactly as a native printer's
does, so those signals fit both cases. The second treated 0 connectors as
decisive -- it was not either, for the same reason: 0 connectors is what
you see both when none is needed and when one is missing. Only putting
paper in the tray separated them.
Operational consequence, now that it is known: there is NO Windows host in
this path. Nothing to keep powered on, nothing to patch, no single point
of failure between Universal Print and the device.
Deliberately NOT checked by the app. Listing connectors needs the
PrintConnector.Read.All scope, and it would tell us less than
isAcceptingJobs and status.state already do -- which the preflight reads.
Adding an admin-consented permission for a weaker signal is a bad trade.
The diagnostic script asks for it; the Function App does not.
